reference: Ncurses tput for standard and independently tic-compiled extended capabilities, with explicit boolean-status/ESC representation adapters. Legacy and wide-number records and directory precedence use independent term(5) contracts; no expected values are sampled from candidate output.
coverage: Standard xterm-256color numeric short and canonical names against tput.
True and false standard boolean capabilities against tput status.
A standard clear-screen string against tput bytes with ESC escaping.
Direct BASHTINFO_PATH file loading for legacy, 32-bit numeric, and extended capability records.
Missing capability and missing terminal error behavior.
Private directory lookup and environment precedence over distinct independently packed entries.
Named extended capabilities are compiled by independent ncurses tic -x, rather than a malformed hand-packed trailer.
exclusions: Database versions beyond legacy, wide-number and extended fixtures are not exhaustively covered; no terminal driver or key-decoding behavior is inferred.

cases.purpose: Compare the standard numeric columns capability with ncurses tput using the same xterm-256color entry.
cases.script:
TERM=xterm-256color; export TERM; unset COLUMNS LINES
if [[ $(type -t tinfo) == builtin ]]; then
  tinfo getnum cols
else
  tput cols
fi

cases.purpose: Compare the long numeric capability name with ncurses tput colors; this also exercises the canonical-name lookup.
cases.script:
TERM=xterm-256color; export TERM; unset COLUMNS LINES
if [[ $(type -t tinfo) == builtin ]]; then
  tinfo getnum max_colors
else
  tput colors
fi

cases.purpose: Compare the true auto-margin boolean; tput reports booleans through status, so the reference adapter emits the documented 0/1 line.
cases.script:
TERM=xterm-256color; export TERM
if [[ $(type -t tinfo) == builtin ]]; then
  tinfo getflag am
else
  if tput am; then
    printf '1\n'
  else
    rc=$?
    if [[ $rc -eq 1 ]]; then printf '0\n'; else exit $rc; fi
  fi
fi

cases.purpose: Compare a false boolean capability to cover the absent/false distinction in the terminfo boolean table.
cases.script:
TERM=xterm-256color; export TERM
if [[ $(type -t tinfo) == builtin ]]; then
  tinfo getflag hc
else
  if tput hc; then
    printf '1\n'
  else
    rc=$?
    if [[ $rc -eq 1 ]]; then printf '0\n'; else exit $rc; fi
  fi
fi

cases.purpose: Compare clear_screen with ncurses tput -x clear, which suppresses the optional clear-scrollback extension, after translating raw ESC bytes to tinfo’s documented escaped representation.
cases.script:
TERM=xterm-256color; export TERM
if [[ $(type -t tinfo) == builtin ]]; then
  tinfo getstr clear_screen
else
  raw=$(tput -x clear)
  raw=${raw//$'\033'/$'\\E'}
  printf '%s\n' "$raw"
fi

cases.purpose: Check the Bash builtin type/help metadata contract without invoking a terminal operation.
Parse an independently packed legacy 0x011A entry through BASHTINFO_PATH as a file; check a number, false/true booleans, a string offset, and ESC escaping.
Parse an independently packed ncurses 0x021E entry and verify a 32-bit columns value above the legacy signed-16-bit range.

Compile a valid extended terminfo entry with independent ncurses tic -x; compare named boolean, numeric and escaped string queries with ncurses tput. Boolean status and ESC escaping adapt only the documented output representation.
cases.script:
mkdir database
printf '%s\n' 'fixture-ext|private fixture,' '  am, cols#42,' '  userbool, usernum#73, userstr=\EZ,' > entry.src
command -p tic -x -o database entry.src
export BASHTINFO_PATH=database TERMINFO=database TERM=fixture-ext
if [[ $(type -t tinfo) == builtin ]]; then
 tinfo getflag userbool
 tinfo getnum usernum
 tinfo getstr userstr
else
 if tput -x userbool; then printf '1\n'; else rc=$?; [[ $rc == 1 ]]; printf '0\n'; fi
 tput -x usernum
 raw=$(tput -x userstr)
 raw=${raw//$'\033'/$'\\E'}
 printf '%s\n' "$raw"
fi

cases.purpose: Verify that a capability absent from a valid standard entry produces no value and a failing tinfo status.
cases.script:
TERM=xterm-256color; export TERM
if tinfo getnum bashos_missing_capability; then
  exit 91
else
  rc=$?
fi
printf '%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Check the documented failed lookup path for a nonexistent terminal name, including a diagnostic and failure status.
cases.script:
if tinfo getnum cols bashos_no_such_terminal; then
  exit 91
else
  rc=$?
fi
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Independent term(5) records in private character and hexadecimal directories verify BASHTINFO_PATH before TERMINFO before TERMINFO_DIRS, ordered fallback, and hex-directory lookup.

Valid tic -x output with a wide standard number selects the 32-bit number format and exercises multiple named capabilities of every type, an empty string, and a wide extended number; tput supplies independent values.
cases.script:
mkdir database
printf '%s\n' 'fixture-many|private extended fixture,' '  am, cols#70000,' '  zflag, aflag, znum#70000, anum#19,' '  ztext=last, atext=first, emptytext=, middlestr=\EZ,' > entry.src
command -p tic -x -o database entry.src
export BASHTINFO_PATH=database TERMINFO=database TERM=fixture-many
if [[ $(type -t tinfo) == builtin ]]; then
 tinfo getflag aflag; tinfo getflag zflag
 tinfo getnum anum; tinfo getnum znum
 for cap in atext emptytext middlestr ztext; do tinfo getstr "$cap" || exit; done
else
 for cap in aflag zflag; do if tput -x "$cap"; then printf '1\n'; else exit 91; fi; done
 tput -x anum; tput -x znum
 for cap in atext emptytext middlestr ztext; do raw=$(tput -x "$cap") || exit; raw=${raw//$'\033'/$'\\E'}; printf '%s\n' "$raw"; done
fi

cases.purpose: A normal inherited string cancellation must not consume bytes in the extended value table or displace later capability names; compare surviving values and cancelled-string failure status with tput.
cases.script:
mkdir database
printf '%s\n' 'fixture-parent|private parent,' '  aflag, anum#17, astr=first, dropstr=old, zstr=last,' 'fixture-child|private child,' '  dropstr@, use=fixture-parent,' > entry.src
command -p tic -x -o database entry.src
export BASHTINFO_PATH=database TERMINFO=database TERM=fixture-child
if [[ $(type -t tinfo) == builtin ]]; then
 tinfo getflag aflag; tinfo getnum anum
 tinfo getstr astr; tinfo getstr zstr
 if tinfo getstr dropstr; then exit 91; else printf 'cancelled=%s\n' "$?"; fi
else
 if tput -x aflag; then printf '1\n'; else exit 91; fi
 tput -x anum
 for cap in astr zstr; do raw=$(tput -x "$cap") || exit; printf '%s\n' "$raw"; done
 if tput -x dropstr; then exit 91; else printf 'cancelled=%s\n' "$?"; fi
fi

cases.purpose: Names begin at offset zero when a valid extended entry has booleans and numbers but no string values.
cases.script:
mkdir database
printf '%s\n' 'fixture-nostr|private no strings,' '  loneflag, lonenum#51,' > entry.src
command -p tic -x -o database entry.src
export BASHTINFO_PATH=database TERMINFO=database TERM=fixture-nostr
if [[ $(type -t tinfo) == builtin ]]; then tinfo getflag loneflag; tinfo getnum lonenum; else if tput -x loneflag; then printf '1\n'; else exit 91; fi; tput -x lonenum; fi

cases.purpose: A name absent from a valid independently compiled extended entry retains the documented tinfo no-value/status1 contract; no tput status-equivalence claim is made for unknown names.
cases.script:
mkdir database
printf '%s\n' 'fixture-parent|private parent,' '  aflag, anum#17, astr=first, dropstr=old, zstr=last,' 'fixture-child|private child,' '  dropstr@, use=fixture-parent,' > entry.src
command -p tic -x -o database entry.src
export BASHTINFO_PATH=database TERMINFO=database TERM=fixture-child
for kind in getflag getnum getstr; do if tinfo "$kind" no_such_private_capability; then exit 91; else printf '%s=%s\n' "$kind" "$?"; fi; done

cases.purpose: A valid inherited cancellation leaves no string-value bytes; capability names must still be read from offset zero.
cases.script:
mkdir database
printf '%s\n' 'fixture-parent|private parent,' '  loneflag, lonenum#29, dropstr=old,' 'fixture-cancel|private cancelled child,' '  dropstr@, use=fixture-parent,' > entry.src
command -p tic -x -o database entry.src
export BASHTINFO_PATH=database TERMINFO=database TERM=fixture-cancel
if [[ $(type -t tinfo) == builtin ]]; then
 tinfo getflag loneflag; tinfo getnum lonenum
 if tinfo getstr dropstr; then exit 91; else printf 'cancelled=%s\n' "$?"; fi
else
 if tput -x loneflag; then printf '1\n'; else exit 91; fi
 tput -x lonenum
 if tput -x dropstr; then exit 91; else printf 'cancelled=%s\n' "$?"; fi
fi
